extracted.intended_audience: zoologists, taxonomists, and students studying freshwater sponges (Spongillidae), especially Indian fauna
extracted.subtask_description: Diagnostic and classificatory criteria for identifying and distinguishing genera and species of freshwater Spongillidæ in India, using gemmule and spicule morphology, skeleton structure, and other morphological characters. Includes keys, genus and species diagnoses, and a glossary of relevant terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order Halichondrina diagnostic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Siliceous monaxon sponges in which the horny skeleton is much reduced or absent and the spicular skeleton is more or less definitely reticulate. The microscleres are usually rod-like and rarely have more than one main axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a higher-order diagnostic frame: presence of siliceous monaxon spicules, reduced/absent horny skeleton, reticulate spicular skeleton, and typically rod-like microscleres help assign a specimen to Halichondrina.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Spongillidæ diagnostic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Freshwater Halichondrina which at certain seasons produce gemmules armed with peculiar microscleres. Two distinct kinds of microsclere are often present, that associated with the gemmule sometimes consisting of a vertical shaft at the ends of which transverse disks or rotulæ are borne. There is always at least a trace of a subdermal cavity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of seasonal gemmules with characteristic microscleres (sometimes two kinds), and at least a trace of a subdermal cavity, are family-level criteria distinguishing freshwater Spongillidæ from related marine families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subfamily division by gemmule-rotules (Spongillinæ vs Meyeninæ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many authors divide the Spongillidæ into two subfamilies:--Spongillinæ (or Euspongillinæ), in which the gemmule-spicules have no transverse rotulæ, and Meyeninæ (or Ephydatiinæ), in which they have rotulæ at one or both ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a primary subfamilial split used in classification, but the text warns the transition is gradual and some species are difficult to assign on this criterion alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key I — microsclere transverse-disk criterion (Spongilla vs Pectispongilla)
rubrics_metrics.description: I. Microscleres without transverse disks. A. Microscleres of the parenchyma similar in general structure to those of the gemmule; the latter without comb-like vertical rows of spines at the ends -> SPONGILLA. B. Microscleres of the gemmule with comb-like vertical rows of spines at both ends -> PECTISPONGILLA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use microsclere morphology (presence/absence of transverse disks; comb-like rows of spines on gemmule microscleres) as the decision point to separate these genera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ephydatia genus diagnostic criterion (birotulate microscleres)
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscleres of the gemmule birotulate, the rotulæ with serrated or strongly sinuous edges; parenchyma spicules usually absent, never of complicated structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If gemmule microscleres are birotulate with strongly serrated/sinuous rotules and parenchyma lacks complex spicules, identify as Ephydatia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dosilia genus diagnostic criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscleres of the gemmule birotulate (as in Ephydatia); microscleres of the parenchyma consisting of numerous shafts meeting in different planes in a central nodule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish Dosilia from Ephydatia by the parenchyma spicule arrangement (numerous shafts meeting in a central nodule) despite similar gemmule microscleres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trochospongilla genus diagnostic criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscleres as in Ephydatia except that the rotulæ of the gemmule-spicules have smooth edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare rotule edge ornamentation: smooth-edged rotulæ point to Trochospongilla rather than Ephydatia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corvospongilla genus diagnostic criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscleres of the gemmule without a trace of rotulæ, those of the parenchyma birotulate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If gemmule microscleres lack rotulæ entirely but parenchyma microscleres are birotulate, assign to Corvospongilla.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key III — Tubella diagnostic criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscleres of the gemmule with a well-developed basal rotule and a vertical shaft ending above in a mere knob -> TUBELLA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The distinctive tubelliform gemmule-spicule (basal rotule + vertical shaft with knob) is diagnostic for Tubella.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus Spongilla diagnosis (diagnostic characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules have (normally) cylindrical or subcylindrical spicules that are sharp or blunt at the ends, without a distinct transverse disk or disks and without comb-like vertical rows of spines. The skeleton is variable in structure, sometimes almost amorphous, sometimes having well-defined radiating and transverse fibres firmly compacted with spongin. Flesh-spicules are often absent; when present they are needle-like and resemble the gemmule-spicules in general structure; they have not even rudimentary rotulæ at their ends. The gemmules either lie free in the substance of the sponge or are attached to its support; sometimes they adhere together in free or attached groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A combination of gemmule-spicule shape (cylindrical/subcylindrical, no transverse disks), skeleton texture, and flesh-spicule form is used to recognize Spongilla; the genus is regarded as primitive and cosmopolitan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key to Indian species — gemmule pneumatic coat, color, and texture (Euspongilla group)
rubrics_metrics.description: I. Gemmule provided with a thick, apparently granular pneumatic coat in which the gemmule-spicules are arranged tangentially or vertically. A. No foraminal tubule. a. Sponge bright green, soft and compressible when fresh, very fragile dry -> lacustris. a'. Sponge white or grey, hard both fresh and dry -> alba.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thick granular pneumatic coat plus sponge colour and fresh/dry texture are primary species-level diagnostics within Euspongilla: color (green vs white/grey) and compressibility/hardness separate S. lacustris and S. alba.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key to Indian species — foraminal tubule presence and skeleton/spicule ornamentation
rubrics_metrics.description: B. A foraminal tubule present. b. Skeleton-spicules smooth. beta. Gemmules free; gemmule-spicules arranged tangentially and horizontally -> proliferens. beta'. Gemmules free; gemmule-spicules arranged vertically or nearly so in a single series -> hemephydatia. beta''. Gemmules firmly fixed to the support of the sponge; gemmule-spicules almost vertical, irregularly arranged, as a rule in more than one series -> travancorica. b'. Skeleton-spicules spiny or irregular in outline. beta'''. Gemmule-spicules tangential and horizontal, without rudimentary rotulæ -> cinerea. beta''''. Gemmule-spicules vertical or nearly so, often with rudimentary rotulæ at the tips -> crateriformis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of a foraminal tubule and the combination of skeleton-spicule ornament (smooth vs spiny), gemmule-spicule orientation (tangential/horizontal vs vertical), gemmule fixation (free vs fixed), and presence/absence of rudimentary rotulæ jointly determine species identifications in this part of the key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgenus Eunapius criterion (polygonal air-spaces in gemmule coats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules surrounded in several layers by distinct polygonal air-spaces with chitinous walls. (Subgenus Eunapius.) A. Gemmules single. Skeleton- and gemmule-spicules smooth, pointed, not very stout -> carteri. B. Gemmules bound together in pairs. Skeleton friable; skeleton-spicules slender -> gemina. C. Gemmules bound together in free groups of more than two or forming a 'pavement-layer' at the base of the sponge. c. Skeleton friable; skeleton-spicules slender -> fragilis. c'. Skeleton very hard and resistant; skeleton-spicules stout -> crassissima.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gemmule-coat microstructure (polygonal air-spaces with chitinous walls) plus gemmule arrangement (single, paired, group/pavement-layer) and skeleton hardness/fibre stoutness are used to separate Eunapius species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgenus Stratospongilla criterion (chitinous membranes with parallel gemmule-spicules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmules without or with irregular pneumatic coat, covered by a chitinous membrane or membranes in which the gemmule-spicules lie parallel to the surface. (Subgenus Stratospongilla.) A. Skeleton-spicules spiny or irregular in outline. a. Skeleton-spicules blunt; gemmules covered by a single chitinous membrane -> indica. a'. Skeleton-spicules sharp; gemmules covered by two chitinous membranes -> bombayensis. B. Skeleton-spicules smooth. Skeleton-spicules sharp; gemmule spicules very irregular in form -> ultima.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence/absence/regularity of a pneumatic coat, presence of one or more chitinous membranes, orientation of gemmule-spicules parallel to the membrane, and spine/smoothness of skeleton-spicules are decisive for Stratospongilla species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmule characters and terminology (for diagnosis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gemmule: a mass of cells packed with food-material, surrounded by at least one horny coat, capable of retaining vitality in unfavourable conditions and finally of giving origin to a new sponge. Foramen: an orifice of the gemmule. Foraminal tubule: a horny tube that surrounds the foramina of some gemmules. Pneumatic coat: a horny or chitinous layer on the surface of the gemmule containing air-spaces; if these spaces are of regular form and arrangement it is 'cellular', if minute and irregular it is 'granular'. Pavement layer: adherent gemmules arranged close together in a single layer at the base of a sponge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These gemmule features (coat type, foramina/foraminal tubule, arrangement) are repeatedly used in the keys and species diagnoses — correct interpretation of these terms is essential for applying the key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spicule morphology and vocabulary used as diagnostic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions provided for technical terms used diagnostically: e.g. Megascleres (larger spicules forming the skeleton), Microscleres (smaller spicules lying free or associated with gemmules), Monaxon (single main axis), Birotulate/rotulate/rotula (spicules bearing transverse disks), Tubelliform (straight shaft with a transverse disk at one end and small knob at the other), Amphioxi/amphistrongyli (rod-like spicules sharp or blunt at both ends).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spicule type, axis number, presence/absence and shape of rotulæ/rotulæ edges, and ornament (smooth, spiny, serrated) are primary morphological characters for genus/species separation; glossary definitions in the text provide the exact meanings used by the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton structure descriptors used diagnostically
rubrics_metrics.description: Skeleton described as reticulate, loose or compact, with definite radiating and transverse fibres held together by spongin; descriptors include 'radiating fibres', 'transverse fibres', 'fibres slender or stout', and degree of spongin compaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skeleton architecture and spongin content (loose vs compact; slender vs stout fibres; friable vs very hard) are repeatedly used alongside spicule/gemmule characters to distinguish taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of composite character sets to delimit closely allied species
rubrics_metrics.description: The species in this subgenus are closely allied and must be distinguished rather by the sum of their peculiarities than by any one character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When single characters conflict or vary, taxonomic decisions should be based on the combined pattern of gemmule morphology, spicule types and ornamentation, skeleton structure, gemmule arrangement, and external colour/texture rather than any lone trait.
